newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas strong next winter, weak in Q3, busy trade.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas strong next winter, weak in Q3, busy trade.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices strengthened slightly next winter, traders and brokers said, but levels were weaker in the near months. And although the volume of trade was high, with a large number of spread trades done, dealers said there were no new fundamental factors driving the market.
Offers over the winter were sparse, traders said. "The gas year has firmed predominantly due to a complete lack of offers," said a trader.

There was good interest for trading the winter quarters as part of a spread, with several deals reported for exchanges between Q4 97 and Q1 98 on one side and Q2 98 and Q3 98 on the other. The winter was valued at between 14.25 and 14.35 pence a therm in these spreads, while the summer was exchanged several times at the same price of 10.525 pence a therm.
The fourth and first quarters both closed up in outright terms, but the increase was marginal. No Q4 trade was recorded on an outright basis.

While the winter was strong, the third quarter of this year weakened again. A single trade was seen at 9.25 pence a therm, below Wednesday's assessed range, and both July on its own and a July/August strip also traded at the same price.
"Q3 is very weak, it's slipped further down," said a trader. The weakness was attributed to offers outnumbering bids rather than to any fundamental change.

"It's back to where it was the day before yesterday," said a trader, pointing out that levels have moved up and down with only small swings over the last few days, with no obvious reason for the minor adjustments.
The IPE followed the same pattern, with the front months softening and both August and September seeing bids below 9.00 pence a therm by the close.

But as on the OTC market, winter prices strengthened, with January and February, the only traded months at 25 lots apiece, moving up by 0.05 pence to 17.00 pence and by 0.235 pence to 11.40 pence respectively.
